text: Code refactoring is the process of improving the structure of existing code without changing what it does. Developers refactor to make code easier to read and understand, which helps teams work faster and avoid mistakes. Good refactoring also reduces technical debt—the hidden problems that build up when code is written quickly. For example, you might rename confusing variables, break a long function into smaller ones, or remove duplicate logic. The key rule is that the program must behave exactly the same after refactoring. Tests help confirm this. Although refactoring takes time, it keeps software healthy and easier to maintain in the future.
